Evidence supports controlled hard-negative sampling, but I found no direct sequential-recommendation comparison establishing TF–IDF mining as superior to uniform sampling or moderate-hardness curricula. [Shi et al., WWW 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.03472) connect hard-negative BPR to partial-AUC optimization and demonstrate that hardness should depend on dataset and target K; this does not establish lexical similarity as the appropriate hardness measure. Stronger sequential precedent: [GNNO, SIGIR 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10047), which mines training-sequence transition neighborhoods and gradually increases difficulty, reporting improvements across three Amazon benchmarks.

Hardness also increases false-negative risk. [SRNS, NeurIPS 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.03376) observes that potential positives can remain consistently high-scoring; its sampler combines informativeness with prediction variability to reduce contamination. Lexical neighbors may be plausible substitutes, while complements may share few words: interpreting TF–IDF similarity as negative relevance is therefore an unverified assumption. [McAuley et al., KDD 2015](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.08839) explicitly distinguish substitutes from complements, but learn those relations using supervised product links and richer information unavailable here; their results do not validate title-based negative labels.

For one HSTU model, defensible mitigations are to exclude every item in each user’s available training history, including items outside the truncated input window; SRNS explicitly samples outside observed interactions. Never inspect held-out labels for exclusions. Proposed ablations: uniform sampling; a uniform-plus-lexical sampler; and the same sampler with warm-up, capped hard-negative frequency, and moderate similarity ranks rather than nearest neighbors. These are hypotheses, not established TF–IDF findings. Training-score variability offers another label-free safeguard. All operate inside one model’s training process; assess novelty against GNNO and SRNS, and select using the fixed macro validation HR@10.
